subject: Root-cause and patch the wrapper host-CPU odd-extent edge-block overrun
scope: Root-cause and minimal source patch for the pinned bionic-vulkan-wrapper host-CPU BCn fallback (bcdec) writing full 4x4 blocks for non-block-aligned copy extents. Patch generated against 3abf48704a4d9303967a0811c0dc8ff8567d613b, applied on top of the repo's srgb-storage.patch, built with the recorded Meson/NDK recipe, and A/B validated with tools/tests/vulkan-wrapper-reference.py odd-extents + partial-region families on a recreated 4 KB API 36 emulator (port 5558) and a recreated 16 KB API 37 emulator (port 5568). No repo file other than the patch and this receipt was written; nothing was committed and nothing was sent upstream.

component.name: bionic-vulkan-wrapper host-CPU BCn decode (bcdec path)
component.scratch_source: <workspace>/staging-oddextent/source (copy of the sRGB-patch scratch source, which is the pinned candidate source + image-create + trace-gate + srgb-storage, plus this patch)

root_cause.summary: BCnDecompression() decodes directly into the mapped staging buffer using a row stride of imageExtent.width texels and the raw block position as the destination offset. For an imageExtent that is not a multiple of 4, the last block column/row is a partial block: the decoder still writes a full 4x4 block. Because the stride is tight (non-block-aligned) the partial edge columns spill into the next rows (in-bounds corruption), and the last partial block row writes past the end of the mapped region (out-of-bounds write relative to the mapped staging range).

file_line_evidence.what: BCnDecompression(format, mappedSrcBase, mappedDst, regions, is_striped) is the host-CPU fallback entry point
height/width taken from regions->imageExtent; int dst_stride = texel_size * width; (tight, non-block-aligned row stride)
block loops: for row += 4 and for x += 4, i.e. always ceil(width/4) x ceil(height/4) full blocks
void *dstPixelBlock = (uint8_t*)mappedDst + y*dst_stride + x*texel_size; direct write into destination with no clipping to width/height
bcdec_bc1/bc2/bc3/__bc4_block/bc7 write the whole 4x4 block through dst_stride
watermark and merged-channel fixups likewise use dst_stride, so the debug paths share the same overrun
HostSideDecompression maps the staging VkDeviceMemory with size = imageExtent.width * imageExtent.height * get_bc_target_size(...) (exactly the tight region size)
calls BCnDecompression(in_format, srcData, dstData, region, is_striped) with that mapped pointer
the staging VkBuffer is sized imageExtent.width * imageExtent.height * get_bc_target_size(...), i.e. h*w*texel bytes; the copy-back VkBufferImageCopy region is the same extent

byte_arithmetic.note: overrun is real but the single in-bounds pixel is decoded correctly, so the readback comparison cannot see it

root_cause.classification: Memory-safety-relevant out-of-bounds write relative to the mapped staging range, plus deterministic in-bounds corruption from the non-block-aligned stride. It is NOT a conformance defect of the Vulkan-level copy: a non-multiple-of-4 imageExtent is out of spec for a block-compressed VkBufferImageCopy, and the tool correctly treats the odd-extent cases as recorded, not conformance claims. The wrapper must still not write out of bounds. In practice the writes stayed within the driver allocation on llvmpipe because VkDeviceMemory sizes/mappings are page-granular and larger than the requested region, so no crash was observed; that backing-store generosity is not guaranteed.
root_cause.in_spec_reasoning: When width % 4 == 0 and height % 4 == 0, dst_stride == 4*texel_size (the block stride), the last block starts exactly at width-4/height-4, and every 4x4 write lands inside the region. The patch's temporary-block path produces the same bytes for that case (dst_stride==image_stride and the copy is a full 4x4 copy), so in-spec output is unchanged.
compute_paths: s3tc.comp and bc7.comp only write in-bounds pixels (their store coordinate comes from the clamped image coordinate per linear pixel); the tool's odd-extent compute and compute-view runs show 0 mismatches at every extent in both phases.
The standard (block-aligned) protocol already exercised by the earlier receipts is unaffected.

hunks.what: add copy_block_texels(): copies only min(4, width-x) x min(4, height-y) in-bounds texels from a decoded 4x4 block into the destination with image_stride; comment explains the overrun
int image_stride = texel_size * width; int dst_stride = texel_size * 4; decode into a 4x4 temporary
uint16_t block_texels[4*4*4]; void *dstPixelBlock = block_texels; (128 bytes, covers up to RGBA16F)
masked/watermarked debug path: copy the in-bounds texels before continue
main path: copy the in-bounds texels after decode (and after the srgb linearisation when srgb-storage.patch is stacked)

patch.semantics: All decode paths (bc1/bc2/bc3, bc4/bc5 fill, bc6h half-float, bc7, masked/watermark debug) now write into a 4x4 temporary with a 4-texel row stride and then copy only the in-bounds texels into the tightly-strided destination. Copy volume is now bounded by width*height*texel_size, matching the mapped staging range; block-aligned extents copy the full 4x4 and are bit-identical to before.

apply_checks.on_top_of_srgb_storage_patch: applies cleanly with --fuzz=0 (srgb-storage.patch first, then odd-extent.patch) - this is the repo's stacking order
apply_checks.reverse_order_stacking: NOT clean: applying odd-extent.patch before srgb-storage.patch makes srgb hunk 2/2 fail because both add code at the same per-block loop tail; the repo applies srgb-storage.patch first, so this does not affect the repo stack. Reported honestly rather than working around it.

tool.evaluator_note: The repo reference tool was being edited concurrently by other work. A scratch copy was used identically for all four phases; it carries one initialisation fix (self.bc6h_reference = None) because the payload builder reads that attribute unconditionally and crashes when only odd-extents/partial-region families are selected (AttributeError observed with the unmodified copy). interpretation.unpatched_host_cpu: Hard mismatches against the clipped independent reference at 5x7 / 13x17 / 63x65: 15 / 36 / 48 per format (BC1 and BC3 identical counts), max channel delta up to 255; 1x1 shows 0 in-bounds mismatches (the single in-bounds pixel decodes correctly) even though the block write still overruns.
interpretation.patched_host_cpu: 0 hard mismatches at every extent and on both page sizes; max channel delta 1 for a small number of pixels (bc1 63x65: 2 pixels; bc3 5x7/13x17/63x65: 8/45/787 pixels), all within the tool's 2-LSB tolerance.
interpretation.residual_1lsb: The remaining +/-1 LSB differences are the pre-existing bcdec-vs-independent-reference palette/alpha rounding difference, not the overrun: the same class appears in the unpatched partial-region bc3 host-cpu run (42 within-tolerance pixels) and in the earlier in-spec receipts (host-cpu ~+/-1 against its reference). Compute/compute-view paths are exactly 0 at every extent.
interpretation.compute_paths: 0 mismatches in both unpatched and patched phases at every odd extent and both page sizes - the patch does not change the compute decode.
interpretation.partial_region: 11/11 per phase pass (16x16 base with an 8x8 patch at offset (8,4); sentinel pixels outside the patch unchanged) in unpatched and patched, 4 KB and 16 KB -> block-aligned/in-bounds behaviour unchanged.
interpretation.rgba8_odd_controls: 8/8 per phase system-loader RGBA8 transfers bit-exact (non-multiple-of-4 extents are legal for uncompressed formats).
interpretation.tool_verdict_caveat: The odd-extents plans are declared expectation='recorded' by the tool because the copy region is out of spec for a block-compressed image; the tool therefore reports them as 'recorded' rather than 'pass' even when there are 0 mismatches. The numbers above are the raw metrics, not the verdict label. The patched tool finding '4 produced pixel mismatches' counts probes with any within-tolerance (+/-1) difference; hard mismatches are 0.

conclusions.summary: The host-CPU BCn fallback no longer writes outside the mapped staging region and no longer corrupts in-bounds pixels for non-block-aligned copy extents. On both 4 KB and 16 KB page-size emulators, hard mismatches at 5x7/13x17/63x65 went from 15/36/48 per format to 0, the compute paths were unchanged (0 mismatches in both phases), and the block-aligned partial-region/sentinel controls still pass.
residual: The remaining +/-1 LSB differences between the bcdec host path and the independent reference are decoder rounding convention, not clipping; they exist within tolerance in in-spec/partial cases too.
The odd-extent VkBufferImageCopy itself is out of spec for block-compressed formats; this patch is robustness/memory-safety hardening of the wrapper's fallback, not a conformance fix.
The overrun's practical severity depends on driver allocation/mapping granularity (llvmpipe tolerated it); a stricter driver or guard pages could fault.
srgb-storage.patch must be applied before odd-extent.patch (repo order); the reverse order is not clean (reported).

limitations: Software Vulkan (Mesa llvmpipe) on both page sizes; no physical Android phone/Adreno/Mali result is claimed.

Only BC1 and BC3 odd extents are exercised by the reference tool's odd-extents family (5x7, 13x17, 1x1, 63x65); BC2/BC4/BC5/BC6H/BC7 partial-extent paths share the same code change but are not runtime-tested with odd extents.
No ASAN/guard-page run: the out-of-bounds write was inferred from source arithmetic and from the in-bounds corruption it causes, not captured by a memory sanitizer.
The partial-region family uses a block-aligned 8x8 patch at offset (8,4) into a 16x16 base; it validates sentinel preservation for in-spec copies, not arbitrary offsets.
No concurrency, sampling/render pipeline, or game workload was exercised; results are transfer-readback only.

The evaluator was a scratch copy of tools/tests/vulkan-wrapper-reference.py (hash above) because the repo tool was being edited concurrently and crashed building the payload for these families without a one-line init fix.
